### Bug Root Cause

The bug is that the TypeScript grammar in `src/languages/typescript.js` does not properly highlight camel-case type parameters as a single token. Instead, it only highlights the initial part (e.g., `Out` in `OutT`) as a type, leaving the rest unstyled. This is likely due to the way the grammar matches built-in types or identifiers, not accounting for user-defined type parameters that use camel-case.

### Bug Location

The bug is in the TypeScript grammar definition in `src/languages/typescript.js`. The grammar needs to be updated to treat type parameters (especially those in camel-case) as a single identifier, not just the initial segment.

### Patch

To fix this, we need to ensure that the grammar for TypeScript highlights type parameters (identifiers in type parameter positions) as a single token, not splitting on camel-case boundaries. This can be done by adding a mode for type parameters or adjusting the built-in highlighting rules to treat identifiers in angle brackets (`<...>`) as type parameters.
